sights.w: The Holland-Ghim Moh district's great hawker centre: opened in 1978, rebuilt in a 2015 facelift and refreshed again in a March-May 2024 renovation, yet still old-school neighbourhood in feel — around 72 cooked-food stalls over a wet market, famous for chwee kueh, braised duck, hor fun and carrot cake, a short walk from Buona Vista MRT.
sights.k: Hawker centre & wet market; most stalls breakfast-to-lunch, some till evening

sights.w: The compact hawker centre at the head of Lorong Mambong, renovated during the pandemic — the wallet-friendly counterpoint to Holland V's bars and cafés, with fried bee hoon, minced-meat noodles, laksa and a back-annexe of newer stalls, steps from Holland Village MRT (CC21).
sights.k: Hawker centre; cheap eats in the middle of Holland V's dining strip

sights.w: The Holland Drive estate's two-storey market and food centre, home to a Michelin Bib Gourmand claypot rice (New Lucky), a Michelin-recognised kway chap (Cheng Heng), Margaret Drive Sin Kee chicken rice and a well-loved Malay breakfast stall — the residents' hawker centre just south of the Holland V bar strip.
sights.k: Hawker centre & wet market; cooked food upstairs
